record.context_brief: Single-exponential algorithms for all Betti numbers
record.original_question: Let S be a semi-algebraic subset of R^k defined by s polynomial equalities and inequalities whose degrees are bounded by d. Is there an algorithm that computes all Betti numbers of S in time single exponential in k? More concretely, can the currently known single-exponential methods for computing only the first l Betti numbers for fixed l be extended to compute the full Betti sequence of S within a single-exponential running time in the ambient dimension?

evidence.quote: Computing Betti Numbers in Single Exponential Time ? Suppose S subset R^k is a semi-algebraic set defined in terms of s polynomials, of degrees bounded by d. One of the most fundamental open questions in algorithmic semi-algebraic geometry, is whether there exists a single exponential (in k) time algorithm for computing the Betti numbers of S.

The best we can do so far is summarized in Theorem 6.10 which gives the existence of single exponential time algorithms for computing the first l Betti numbers of S for any constant l. A big challenge is to extend these ideas to design an algorithm for computing all the Betti numbers of S.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ be a semi-algebraic set, defined as a Boolean combination of polynomial equalities and inequalities involving $s$ polynomials in $\mathbb{R}[X_1,\dots,X_k]$, each of degree at most $d$. For each $i \ge 0$, let $b_i(S) = \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_i(S;\mathbb{Q})$ denote the $i$-th Betti number of $S$ (with respect to singular homology with rational coefficients). The input size of $S$ is measured by $s$, $d$, $k$, and the bit-size of the coefficients of the defining polynomials.

An algorithm running on a real RAM (or in the bit complexity model with appropriate adjustments) is said to have single-exponential complexity in $k$ if its running time is bounded by $(sd)^{k^{O(1)}}$.

It is known that:
(i) the zeroth Betti number $b_0(S)$ (the number of connected components) and the first Betti number $b_1(S)$ can each be computed in single-exponential time in $k$;
(ii) more generally, for every fixed nonnegative integer $\ell$, there exists an algorithm with complexity $(sd)^{k^{O(\ell)}}$ that computes the sequence $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_\ell(S)$;
(iii) a doubly-exponential algorithm (e.g.\ via cylindrical algebraic decomposition) computes all Betti numbers $b_0(S),\dots,b_k(S)$.

Question: Does there exist an algorithm that, given as input a description of a semi-algebraic set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}^k$ as above, computes all Betti numbers $b_0(S), b_1(S), \dots, b_k(S)$ in time single-exponential in $k$ (i.e.\ bounded by $(sd)^{k^{O(1)}}$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is widely regarded as a major open question in algorithmic semi-algebraic geometry. Single-exponential algorithms are known only for the first $\ell+1$ Betti numbers for any fixed constant $\ell$ (with complexity $(sd)^{k^{O(\ell)}}$), and recent work (through 2024) extends this to compute bases of the first $\ell$ homology groups and induced maps, but no single-exponential algorithm computing all Betti numbers (especially the middle-dimensional ones) has been found; the only known algorithms for the full Betti sequence remain doubly exponential.

status_evidence.title: Computing the first few Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets in single exponential time
status_evidence.snippet: An algorithm with complexity (sd)^{k^{O(ℓ)}} outputs the first ℓ+1 Betti numbers; previously single-exponential algorithms were known only for the Euler–Poincaré characteristic and b_0, b_1.
status_evidence.claim: Only the first few Betti numbers are known to be computable in single-exponential time.

status_evidence.title: Computing the Homology Functor on Semi-algebraic Maps and Diagrams
status_evidence.snippet: Developing an algorithm for computing the Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets with singly exponential complexity has been a holy grail in algorithmic semi-algebraic geometry and only partial results are known.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024 the full problem remains a 'holy grail' open problem with only partial results.

status_evidence.title: Betti Number Bounds, Applications and Algorithms (Basu)
status_evidence.snippet: Computing the Betti numbers of semi-algebraic sets in single exponential time is an important open problem; doubly exponential algorithms are known via triangulation/CAD.
status_evidence.claim: Computing all Betti numbers in single-exponential time remains open.
